brief.case_against: The record of how much searching preceded this entry is wrong, and the project's rules make that record a condition of promotion. The experiment code scores fourteen variations against the reference; the report and the entry both say thirteen and claim every look was counted. One variation's results — across three time horizons and six assets — are unaccounted for: either it ran and was left off the ledger, or the ledger misdescribes what ran. Because exactly one irreversible read of the held-out data is at stake, the project counts every prior look so the final test is written knowing how big the search was; a ledger that undercounts cannot support promotion until it is reconciled. Two further weaknesses are real, though the entry discloses them itself: the supporting evidence sits mostly in the 2010–2011 crisis years, and the two relevant variations showed essentially zero predictive skill before 2018, so the read is a long shot. On everything else — prediction written before the look, episode floor, whole-holdout slice, confound test — the entry checks out.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a genuine drawdown and the project's stress flag is on, gold's moves over the following one to four weeks spread out in both directions — larger gains and larger losses — by more than gold's own recent turbulence can explain. In pre-2018 data the typical range of outcomes was about a third to a half wider than on similar stressed days without the flag, and about a fifth wider after adjusting for volatility. The entry claims nothing about which way gold goes, only that its range widens. It asks to spend the project's single read of post-2018 data testing whether the pattern holds, with a minimum-sample rule and a volatility control fixed in advance.
brief.what_would_change_it: Reconcile the count. Either produce the fourteenth variation's results and add them to the ledger, or show from the harness record that it never ran and correct the line, then resubmit for a fresh audit stamped to the corrected text. Nothing else in the entry blocks promotion: the prediction, the volatility control and the sample floor were all fixed before the data were looked at, and every quoted number matches the committed report. My residual concern about the evidence would be answered if the held-out read itself lands on enough distinct stress episodes — the floor is eight — spread across the post-2018 years rather than concentrated in one crisis, with the width gap surviving both volatility adjustments as it did before 2018. If the missing variation cannot be accounted for, the entry should not be promoted however clean the rest looks.

brief.case_against: The entry's headline — that its pre-registered prediction held — is false as the record stands. The prediction committed on 25 September, before any data was looked at, required the stressed-and-fragile gold cell's typical outcome range to be at least 1.4 times the normal cell's at all three horizons. The test run on 26 September came back at roughly 1.31, 1.39 and 1.52: it failed the registered bar at two of three horizons. The next day the entry was edited to demand only 1.2, and it now declares the prediction 'held' and 'committed on 2026-09-25'. Moving a threshold to fit data already seen, then presenting it as pre-registered, is exactly the goalpost move these rules exist to catch; the honest move, per the project's own H-008 precedent, was to label the lowered threshold 'seen'. Even setting that aside: the two arms show almost no overall skill in exploration, far under the bar a sealed read must clear, and the evidence rests on 11 stress episodes, seven of them in 2010–2011.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a drawdown of at least five percent and the project's fragility alarm is firing, gold's returns over the following one to four weeks spread out in both directions — bigger gains and bigger losses — by more than gold's own recent volatility explains. The claim concerns only how wide gold's range of outcomes becomes, never which way gold goes. The entry asks for one sealed test: whether conditioning on this state predicts gold's outcome range better than no conditioning, and better than the volatility forecast the project already uses, with a mechanism check that the widening survives after dividing out two different measures of the volatility knowable at the time.
brief.what_would_change_it: Restore the registered 1.4 threshold, record openly that it failed at two of three horizons, and re-label the 1.2 version 'seen' — the project's own flag for a threshold written after the data. The separate mechanism clause (a volatility-adjusted width ratio of at least 1.15 under both volatility yardsticks) was genuinely fixed before the look and did hold, so an entry rewritten to say honestly which number was registered and which was fitted could be re-audited on its merits. The arm-count discrepancy — 13 arms in the report versus 14 in the harness as it stands today — should be reconciled against the harness's history. A sealed read that then clears the full class bar, including beating the existing volatility forecast, would show the concern wrong.

findings.claim: The mechanism clause retains an accidental-pass channel: both σs are backward-looking, so if the OR flag tends to fire early in a stress spell while gold's volatility is still ramping, Elevated forward windows mechanically out-run either σ while late-spell Normal days are already covered by theirs. A within-episode contrast (flag-on vs flag-off days inside the same spell) would close this; the clause as written does not require one.
findings.evidence: Entry §2 names the lag version of this channel itself — "har_scaled ... lags a jump in Gold's vol, so a state that fires at the start of stress spells could clear the ratio on that lag alone" — and answers it with "Gold's trailing 10-day realized σ ... which catches a jump within days." A 10-day trailing σ still lags a multi-day ramp at the 20-day horizon, which is where the raw split is largest (report §4, h=20: raw ratio ≈1.52 vs standardized 1.23–1.29). §9 question 5 asks for "the contrast that only the mechanism produces — within-episode"; the clause is within-bin, across episodes.

brief.case_against: One decisive procedural problem, one substantive. Procedural: the single rehearsal look behind this entry did not stop at the 2018 seal the entry itself commits to. Its committed report states a slice running to June 2019 — eighteen months into the holdout — and prints, year by year, how many stressed days and distinct stress spells fall in 2018 and 2019, split by the fragility alarm. Anyone deciding whether to spend the one irreversible read therefore does so already knowing roughly how many target episodes the first stretch of the sealed window contains. The project's first rule is that exploration never touches the sealed slice; the entry presents this look as clean and nowhere discloses the breach. The arithmetic indicates the headline numbers were computed on pre-2018 dates only, so a re-run with a pre-seal end date would fix it — but as committed, the seal is broken. Substantive: the fragility-conditioned arm's rehearsal skill is a small fraction of the required margin, every uncertainty interval spans zero, and the claim covers about one day in eleven. The pattern looks real, but the odds this read clears an all-days skill bar look poor — and the read cannot be undone.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a meaningful slump and a separate "market is fragile" alarm is ringing, gold's moves over the following one to four weeks spread out in both directions — larger gains and larger losses — by more than gold's own recent turbulence can explain. On rehearsal data from before 2018, that spread was about a third to a half wider than on stressed days when the alarm was silent, and about a fifth wider even after dividing out what a standard volatility forecast already knew. The entry claims nothing about direction: gold is not predicted to rise or fall. It asks for one test on untouched data from 2018 onward, under a bar agreed in advance that also requires beating the project's existing volatility forecast, with a minimum sample of 150 days and 8 distinct stress episodes.
brief.what_would_change_it: Procedurally: re-run the rehearsal look with an end date before 2018, recommit the report so no post-2017 numbers (including the by-year episode counts) sit in the record, restate the ledger, and reconcile the arm count — the report counts 13 tested arms where the harness has 14. That removes the seal objection, and the rest of the entry is sound: the prediction, the pass/fail thresholds and the sample floor were all written down before the look, and every quoted number matches the committed report. Substantively, only the sealed read itself can answer the low-prior concern: it would need to beat both the plain unconditional distribution and the existing volatility forecast on gold's three quantiles by the agreed margin, with the wider-both-sides pattern surviving the volatility adjustment, on at least 150 days spanning 8 distinct stress episodes.

findings.evidence: Entry §2, 'What would test it': 'the confirm read: on stressed, OR-Elevated days, the share of days on which Gold's 20-day forward change is positive, against a coin-flip 50%. A share above 55% on the sealed slice, with a binomial interval clear of 50%, is the bar'. brief.case_against: The entry calls itself a claim about how widely Gold's outcomes spread, but the test it asks to spend the single sealed read on is a bet on direction: the share of stressed, fragile days on which Gold is higher twenty days later, required above 55%. A share of up-days against 50% is an up/down forecast with a confidence attached — the thing the project's rules forbid in any wording — and it contradicts the entry's own mechanism ('the flag should say nothing about which way Gold goes') and its own 'not claimed' list. No pre-registered class bar exists for that test; the entry wrote its own threshold, and its own practice-slice numbers fail the class bar that does exist. The record is unreliable too: the ledger counts 13 arms where the harness ships 14, and it omits that the same Gold width structure was examined under an earlier entry whose location half failed two days before this one was drafted — the failed half was dropped and the surviving half re-registered as 'pre-registered'. The read would not measure what the entry claims, on a ledger that undercounts what was already seen.
brief.what_it_claims: On days when the stock market sits at least five percent below its peak and the project's stress flag is on, Gold's moves over the following one to four weeks are claimed to spread out in both directions — unusually large gains and losses at once — by more than Gold's own recent turbulence explains, while saying nothing about which way Gold will go. On the practice data (before 2018) the spread on those days was about a third to a half wider than on merely-stressed days, and about a fifth wider after stripping out Gold's own volatility, measured over 169 days forming 11 separate stress episodes.
brief.what_would_change_it: Three things. First, a confirm test that actually measures the claim: a width test on Gold's forward distribution judged against the class bar that already exists — beat the plain unconditional benchmark and the project's own volatility forecast, interval clear of zero — or, if that bar cannot apply, a new class bar for width claims written before any candidate is on the table, not a threshold invented inside the entry. Second, a complete ledger: all fourteen arms the harness runs, and the earlier entries that already examined the same Gold width tables, with the prediction honestly re-labelled 'seen' if it was. Third, evidence the effect is not carried by a couple of episodes — the practice data lean heavily on 2010–2011 (seven of eleven stress episodes) — such as per-episode width ratios. If a direction test is ever proposed, it needs its own class bar written in advance — and passing it would contradict this entry's stated mechanism, not confirm it.

brief.case_against: The entry's own rule says a cell needs at least eight separate stress episodes to count as a measurement. The evidence it rests on has two. In the pre-2018 data, the alarm-on stressed cell is 169 trading days drawn from exactly two episodes: the 2011 crash (145 days) and one 2015 spell (24 days). Every number the entry presents as a success — the spread being 1.3 to 1.5 times wider, and still 15 to 29 percent wider after volatility is divided out — comes from those two episodes. The entry tells the reader the cell clears its size floor by quoting the day count (169 against a floor of 150) and never mentions the episode count (two against a floor of eight), the number its own standard cares about most. If the post-2018 tape behaves like the pre-2018 tape, the sealed test will likely come back 'too small to read', spending the project's single irreversible look. Separately, the ledger says thirteen signal variants were run; the code's vocabulary says fourteen were scored, so the look count is wrong.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a stressed patch (down at least five percent from its peak) and the project's fragility alarm is ringing, gold's outcomes over the following one to four weeks spread out in both directions — unusually large gains and unusually large losses — by more than gold's own recent volatility can explain. The claim is deliberately not about direction: the alarm should say nothing about whether gold rises or falls. The entry asks for one test on the sealed post-2018 data: on stressed days, the alarm-on days' middle-half spread of gold outcomes must be at least 1.2 times the alarm-off days', and at least 1.15 times after each day's move is divided by either of two volatility yardsticks known at the time. A result on fewer than 150 days or eight distinct stress episodes is declared too small in advance; the test runs once and is published either way.
brief.what_would_change_it: Disclosure first: the entry must say in its own text that the supporting cell is two episodes — below its own eight-episode floor — while the comparison cell has twenty-seven. Then either justify the spend anyway, by showing the volatility-adjusted widening holds within each episode separately rather than only pooled across two, or re-scope the sealed test so it proceeds only if its own cell clears the episode floor, with an honest case that the post-2018 tape contains enough alarm-on stress episodes (2018, 2020 and 2022 are the candidates) to make that likely. Finally, fix the multiplicity ledger: state fourteen scored variants to match the code, or pin the harness version that produced thirteen, so every look is counted. With those changes this is a clean, well-built width hypothesis; without them the owner would be buying an irreversible read on the strength of two episodes, told as if they were a measurement.

brief.case_against: The entry's record of what was looked at is wrong twice. First, the report behind it was run at least twice: once on the evening of 25 September with different settings (different stress bin edges and a lower minimum cell size), and once on 26 September with the settings the entry quotes. The ledger lists only the second run, calls it 'the first look specific to this entry', and claims the settings were 'as the harness shipped it' — yet the settings changed after that first run, and what the first run showed is recorded nowhere. Second, the ledger says the run scored thirteen signal variants; the harness scores fourteen. One variant's look is unaccounted for. The project's core rule is that every look is counted before promotion; this entry breaks it twice, and the gaps sit exactly where tuning-after-seeing would hide. Beyond the record: the supporting evidence is eleven stress spells concentrated in 2010-11 and 2015-16, the effect roughly halves once gold's own volatility is divided out, and by the entry's own numbers the sealed test's skill bar looks out of reach.
brief.what_it_claims: When the stock market is in a real drawdown (down at least five percent) and the project's fragility alarm is ringing, gold's moves over the following one to four weeks spread out more in both directions — bigger gains and bigger losses — than gold's own recent volatility can explain. It claims nothing about which way gold goes. On the pre-2018 exploration data, gold's middle spread in alarm periods was about one-and-a-third to one-and-a-half times wider than in calm-alarm-free stress days, shrinking to about a fifth to three-tenths wider after volatility is divided out. The entry asks for exactly one read on the sealed 2018-onward data, scoring gold's predicted quartile range against a no-information baseline and against the project's existing volatility forecast, with a pre-set minimum of 150 days and eight distinct stress episodes, the result published either way.
brief.what_would_change_it: Fix the ledger. Record the 25 September run — its settings and what it showed — or show why it was not a look at this question; reconcile the variant count (thirteen versus fourteen) so every arm's run is either counted or shown not to have happened; and restate the configuration history honestly instead of 'as the harness shipped it'. If the missing run is consistent with what the entry reports and the missing variant is explained, the blocking defects are cured: the prediction, the floor and the slice were all written before the look the entry reads, and every number I checked matches the committed report. The remaining doubts are ones only the sealed read can settle: whether the effect holds outside the 2010-11 and 2015-16 stress clusters, and whether a width effect confined to about one day in eleven can clear a skill bar scored over all days. A clean ledger plus a sealed cell of eight or more distinct episodes still holding the width ratio would answer both.
